text:
Carla Gomez: Heads up — we started the bootguard/firmware roll for rack-r11 in us-west-2 at 09:05 UTC and a small subset toggled secure boot unexpectedly. Not a full bricked state but several nodes failed to boot into the GPU pool.
Devon Li: seeing it on the dashboard, GPU pool available capacity dropped ~12% and provisioning latency spiked. Which batch?
Carla Gomez: batch 3, image fw-2026-03-19-bootguard. Affected nodes are 11-16 in rack-r11, hit both A100 and H100 machines.
Marta Singh: tagging @SRE Oncall Bot — can you run the quick health check and gather journalctl from the failed nodes? Also which fallback policy kicked in?
SRE Oncall Bot: running runbook: infra/firmware/bootguard-triage v2. Collecting logs from nodes r11-11..r11-16. ETA ~2m.
Devon Li: initial metric: secureboot=1 -> bootloader rejected unsigned PXE chain on 5 of 6 nodes. The loader reported UEFI var lock mismatch.
Carla Gomez: we definitely didn't expect var-lock toggles. Patch notes said 'UEFI policy tighten' but not var-lock flips.
Marta Singh: can we force fallback to legacy provisioning for now? We have a backlog of customer jobs waiting. Cost impact if we shift to other regions?
Devon Li: fallback policy ALLOWED fallback-to-us-west-1. Replicating jobs will add cross-region egress and startup GPU warmup; estimated cost ~ $1.2k/hr at current load. Latency SLOs will degrade for some customers.
Carla Gomez: prefer to avoid cross-region unless we have to. What's the risk of rolling the cluster back to previous firmware?
Marta Singh: rollback via the orchestrator is nontrivial — the image signer changed; we might need a manual NVram clear step in the BMC to reset UEFI vars. That requires out-of-band access; could be parallelized but takes ~8m/node with our current OOB throughput.
Devon Li: can we script the NVram clear? Something like:
```
ipmitool -H $BMC -U $USER -P $PASS chassis bootdev pxe && 
ssh root@$NODE 'efi-reset-vars --force'
```
But ipmitool sessions are limited, and we've hit session quotas before.
Carla Gomez: we already have ipmi session saturation alerts for us-west-2 from last week. We should throttle and stagger.
SRE Oncall Bot: session_count(us-west-2) = 48 (threshold 50). Recommend rate_limit 6/s.
Marta Singh: action plan proposal: 1) Pause next firmware batch 2) Stagger NVram clears using 4 parallel BMC sessions 3) Re-enable provisioning fallback to local legacy image (non-signed) for the 8m window 4) Notify customers and put a temporary capacity headroom target.
Devon Li: +1. Also suggest we boot one node into diagnostic mode to capture a full UEFI trace for the firmware vendor. Don't want to blind-roll.
Carla Gomez: I'm going to open a vendor ticket and include trace. Also will create a canary with a different microcode build on a spare rack (r14) to validate var-lock behavior.
Marta Singh: deployment note: increase dedicated pool buffer to 20% for the next 3 hours to avoid evictions. That will increase reserved capacity cost ~ $600 for the window. Approve?
Devon Li: approve. Please add cost center tag infra-emergency.
Carla Gomez: pinging #support to update customers impacted by us-west-2 delay. Draft message: "We're investigating a firmware-related boot issue affecting a small number of GPU hosts in us-west-2; jobs may be delayed up to 30 minutes. We're prioritizing minimal disruption and will post updates"
SRE Oncall Bot: logs collected: r11-13 journal excerpt -> "EFI_VAR_WATCHDOG: var-lock mismatch detected, secureboot status set to 1". Attaching trace id 8f3a2b.
Devon Li: good, that's actionable. We'll need the vendor firmware team to explain why nvram locking changed without a signing policy update.
Marta Singh: next steps assigned: Carla -> vendor ticket + canary setup; Devon -> NVram clear runbook + ipmi throttle script; I'll coordinate capacity buffer & customer comms.
Carla Gomez: thanks. If rollback can't be automated cleanly we will route critical workloads to dedicated fallback hosts (no secureboot) and autoscale the reserved pool to handle the delta.
Devon Li: I'll start the NVram clear script in a throttled loop now against r11-11..r11-16, will post back on success/fail counts.
SRE Oncall Bot: deploy-bot detected new job: canary-deploy on r14 at 09:27 UTC.
Carla Gomez: update — NVram clear succeeded on 3/6 nodes, 2 failed during ssh step (network timeout), 1 still pending. Continuing with staggered retries.
Marta Singh: thank you. We'll reconvene in 20m or earlier if major changes. :thumbsup:
